evidence.quote: today the Federal Open Market Committee decided to leave our policy interest rate unchanged.
For the time being, we're well positioned to wait for greater clarity before considering any adjustments to our policy stance.
We don't think we need to be in a hurry. We think we can be patient.
The risks of higher unemployment and higher inflation appear to have risen
Our obligation is to keep longer-term inflation expectations well anchored and to prevent a one-time increase in the price level from becoming an ongoing inflation problem.
So the economy itself is still, you know, in solid shape.

parsed.rationale: Rates held with a firm, patient wait-and-see stance that resists preemptive cuts, citing above-target inflation and tariff risks, while acknowledging two-sided risks to employment and inflation. On net the signal is balanced with a slight hawkish tilt from the reluctance to ease.
